statement.p: Jerome is conducting market research on the cost of auto insurance. Jerome has determined that the average annual cost of auto insurance is 1346, and that the distribution of costs is normally distributed with a standard deviation of 53.
a. Find the probability that a single randomly selected consumer spends more than 1442 on auto insurance.
b. The cost of the middle 60 of auto insurance policies falls between (round to the nearest dollar):
c. The most expensive 8 of auto insurance policies cost at least how much annually?

solution.p: Define the normal distribution in Desmos: \displaystyle\text{normaldist}{\left({1346},{53}\right)}.
a. In Desmos, select RIGHT region, compute AREA. Enter the boundary 1442 and obtain the probability: \displaystyle{P}{\left({x}\geq{1442}\right)}={0.035}.

b. For the middle 60 of the data, select INNER region, compute BOUNDS. Enter the area of the middle region \displaystyle{0.60} and obtain the upper and lower bounds: \displaystyle{1301}\leq{x}\leq{1391} .
Alternatively (old Desmos approach): split the remaining region between the tails and find the boundaries:

c. For the most expensive 8 of the distribution, need \displaystyle{0.08} of the area to the right. Use a RIGHT region, compute BOUNDS and enter the area to the right \displaystyle{0.08}. Obtain the lower bound: \displaystyle{x}={1420}.
Alternatively (old Desmos approach): use the inverse function with the area needed to the LEFT:
